# Home

## The Musée des impressionnismes Giverny is preparing to reopen to the public for the 2027 season.

Upcoming exhibition: Bonnard-Vuillard. Abolir le hasard

from March 26 to July 4, 2027

[See more](https://www.mdig.fr/en/exhibitions/bonnard-vuillard/)

The Musée des impressionnismes Giverny is a major site of Impressionism in Normandy, which presents innovative temporary exhibitions in an exceptional surrounding combining art and nature, 1 hour from Paris and Rouen. 

## Practical information

To see the opening days and times, click on the link below.

[Plan your visit](https://www.mdig.fr/en/plan-your-visit/opening-times-and-access-2/)

## Tickets

You can buy your tickets on site, at the entrance of the museum, or save time by buying your skip-the-line tickets online.

[Buy tickets](https://l.mdig.fr/Buy-Tickets-Online-2026)

## Calendar of activities

Guided tours, readings, events… See activities to do alone, with family or friends.

[See activities](https://www.mdig.fr/en/exhibitions-and-activities/activities/)

[Come in groups](https://www.mdig.fr/en/plan-your-visit/group-visits-to-the-museum/)

[**Discover the museum’s garden**\\ \\ Located just a few metres from Monet’s home and gardens, see more about the museum’s garden](https://www.mdig.fr/en/the-museum/the-garden/)

## Live from the museum

- facebook

 [See the post](https://www.facebook.com/475243767967535/posts/1604781755013725)

 \[Ce jour-là\] 🎂 Le saviez-vous ? Claude Monet est né au cœur de la future grande rue des marchands de tableaux de Paris ! L’artiste voit le jour le 14 novembre 1840 au 45, rue Laffitte, dans le 9e arrondissement de Paris, au pied de la butte Montmartre. Si le marché de l’art y balbutie encore à sa naissance, la rue devient célèbre à partir des années 1860 pour concentrer une grande partie des galeries…

 November 14

 [See the post](https://www.facebook.com/475243767967535/posts/1604781755013725)

- instagram

 [See the post](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfpmKLwxkF1/)

 \[Démontage\] L’heure est venue de décrocher les œuvres de la collection du musée ! Après avoir fait l’objet d’un constat d’état, elles retournent dans les réserves en attendant leur prochain accrochage. La collection du musée demeure toutefois accessible en ligne sur mdig.fr, rubrique « La collection en ligne » [#Demontage](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/Demontage) [#Exposition](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/Exposition) [#Impressionnisme](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/Impressionnisme) [#Giverny](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/Giverny) [#Musee](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/Musee)

 #Braderie | Envie de faire de bonnes affaires ? Rendez-vous ce week-end à la braderie du musée ! Profitez de 10% à 50% de réduction sur une sélection de produits : livres, carnets, catalogues, objets déco, bijoux… 🗓️ Samedi 14 et dimanche 15 novembre de 10h à 18h

 November 10

 [See the post](https://bsky.app/profile/museegiverny.bsky.social/post/3mzxdkobh6c27)

- facebook

 [See the post](https://www.facebook.com/475243767967535/posts/1600752752083292)

 \[11 novembre\] « Quant à moi, je reste ici quand même, et, si ces sauvages doivent me tuer, ce sera au milieu de mes toiles, devant l’œuvre de toute ma vie » Claude Monet, 1914. Au début de la Première Guerre mondiale, alors que les troupes allemandes approchent de la région et que beaucoup d’habitants fuient Giverny, Monet refuse de quitter sa maison et ses ateliers. Il poursuit la réalisation de ses grands “Nymphéas”, trouvant…

 November 11

 [See the post](https://www.facebook.com/475243767967535/posts/1600752752083292)

- instagram

 [See the post](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfaHqWfAYS9/)

 \[[#TroisMatsGiverny\]](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/TroisMatsGiverny]) Merci à tous les donateurs ! 🙏 La campagne de financement participatif, lancée à l’occasion du centenaire de la mort de Claude Monet, s’est achevée le 1er novembre 2026. Grâce à la formidable mobilisation de nos donateurs, ainsi qu’au précieux soutien du Cercle des Mécènes du musée des impressionnismes Giverny et des Amis du musée, plus de 50 000 € ont été collectés ! Nous adressons nos remerciements les plus chaleureux à toutes celles…

##### Welcome to the

# Pinakothek der Moderne

## Under One Roof: Four Museums

Housing four museums under one roof devoted to art, works on paper, architecture and design, the Pinakothek der Moderne ranks as one of the greatest collectors of artworks in Europe. Its trans-disciplinary approach – as expressed in its concept of “four-in-one” – is both visionary and, for the most part, unique.

Ever since it was founded, the Pinakothek der Moderne has continued to offer a single ticket that allows visitors to discover all four of the art disciplines on display, to develop new perspectives and to experience them in all their diversity and topicality. The central feature of the Pinakothek der Moderne complex is its imposing glass rotunda, which serves as a vibrant place of encounter and acts as point of departure for the continual stream of exhibitions, tours and cultural events.

The Pinakothek der Moderne as a forum for exploring current trends wishes its visitors many inspiring moments and an exciting stay!

#### Experience the full diversity of four disciplines

[To the museums](https://www.pinakothek-der-moderne.de/en/the-four-museums/) [Our program](https://www.pinakothek-der-moderne.de/programm/) [Our events](https://www.pinakothek-der-moderne.de/events/)

### Pinakothek der Moderne

## A vibrant place of diversity

Four museums under one roof present exhibitions of pioneering international architects, designers and artists of the highest quality. Regardless of age, gender, origin or social background, the Pinakothek der Moderne brings people together, encourages reflection, promotes social discourse and conveys education and values. An open meeting place with activities of all kinds in and around the building - sophisticated, inviting, entertaining.

## OPEN4

### ENGAGE - EXPLORE - CREATE

Welcome to OPEN4, the Pinakothek der Moderne's education and outreach programme.

We want to create new encounters, encourage people to join in and make the four museums with art, prints & drawings, architecture and design an experience for everyone. Our programme invites visitors of all ages to discover the collections and special exhibitions of the Pinakothek der Moderne in diverse and creative ways and to gain new perspectives.

- ## Conférence déambulée : « Des images plein la tête »

 Partez pour une déambulation originale dans nos images mentales à travers les œuvres du musée

 Dimanche 15 novembre – 10h30

 [Inscrivez-vous](http://augustins.toulouse.fr/semaine-du-cerveau-des-images-plein-la-tete/)

- ## Conférence avec l’association Les Amis du musée des Augustins

 La directrice du musée des Augustins Laure Dalon et l’artiste Nicolas Dhervillers animeront une conférence intitulée « La Part des anges : De la genèse du projet à l’exposition dans le parcours du musée ».

 Mercredi 18 novembre – 18 heures

 [Inscrivez-vous](https://www.amis-des-augustins.fr/)

- ## Nocturne : Art et créativité

 Le musée s’ouvre en mode atelier de création & rencontre avec l’artiste Nicolas Dhervillers

 Jeudi 19 novembre – 18 heures

 [Réservez votre soirée](http://augustins.toulouse.fr/nocturne-art-et-creativite-2288144/)

- ## Votre avis nous intéressent !

 Pour nous aider à faire évoluer notre magazine et à construire les prochains numéros, nous vous invitons à partager vos idées, vos suggestions et vos attentes…

 Questionnaire

 [En savoir plus](https://augustins.toulouse.fr/2026/10/22/aidez-nous-a-ameliorer-notre-magazine/)

- ## Réouverture des salles gothiques

 Le musée des Augustins poursuit sa métamorphose, c’est au tour des salles gothiques de retrouver le public depuis le samedi 3 octobre.

 Évènement

 [En savoir plus](https://augustins.toulouse.fr/2026/09/10/les-salles-gothiques-rouvrent-au-public/)

- ## Exposition « La Part des anges »

 Le musée donne carte blanche à l’artiste Nicolas Dhervillers pour l’exposition « La Part des anges ». Son travail à la fois intense et poétique est à découvrir jusqu’au 22 février 2027.

 Jusqu’au 22 février 2027

 [En savoir plus](https://augustins.toulouse.fr/2026/09/10/nicolas-dhervillers-la-part-des-anges/)

## Information for your visit

### How to find us

Our [map (PDF)](https://www.pinakothek.de/media/6729/download/BSTGS_Lageplan_241022.jpg?v=1 'Lageplan der Pinakotheken') gives you an overview of the different ways to reach us.

Alte Pinakothek 
Barer Strasse 27 
(Entrance Theresienstrasse) 
80333 Munich

You can reach the Alte Pinakothek by:

Tram  
Line 27 | 28: Stop Pinakotheken

Underground 
U2: Stop Königsplatz or Theresienstrasse 
U3 | U6: Odeonsplatz or Universität  
U4 | U5: Odeonsplatz

Bus 
Line 100 (museum line) | Line 58 (CityRing) : Stop Pinakotheken

We recommend travelling by public transport, as there are no parking spaces available in the immediate vicinity of the museums.

### Orientation and barrier-free access

[Orientation plan download (PDF)](https://www.pinakothek.de/media/8129/download/BSTGS_Orientierungsflyer_web.pdf?v=5)

**Entrance to the museum**  
Barrier-free access possible at the main entrance.

**Parking**  
On the north side of the Alte Pinakothek. Access from Arcis- and Barerstrasse.  
Ring the bell at the gate and present a disabled parking permit.

**Lifts**  
There are four lifts in the museum. All exhibition areas as well as the café and the museum shop are barrier-free.

**Seating and wheelchairs**  
Light, portable folding chairs and two wheelchairs are available. Please ask at the information desk.

**Restrooms**  
Disabled toilets are located on the ground floor.

**Cloakrooms and lockers** 
The cloakroom is located on the ground floor. Jackets and bags can be deposited for a fee of 1 Euro per person. Lockers are also available (deposit 1 or 2 euros). Spacious lockers are available for school classes. The key is available at the information desk.

**Information**  
+49 (0)89 23805 216 (cash desk/information desk, available during regular opening hours) 
+49 (0)89 23805 284 or [info@pinakothek.de](mailto:info@pinakothek.de) (Information and Service Department, available MON-FRI)

### Pocket Guide | Alte Pinakothek Unframed

The WebApp is your digital companion through the museum, whether before, during or after your visit. There are currently six tours for adults, four tours especially for children and a tour in easy language. 

But the possibilities go much further: Using your own area with saved works, you can create completely individualised tours and also explore the collection in new depth thanks to the tagging of the paintings. Try it out for yourself!

**Now available for free on your mobile phone via** [**www.app.pinakothek.de**](https://www.app.pinakothek.de/)**!**

### Publications

All publications are available at the [museum shop Cedon](https://museumsshop.cedon.de/Kataloge/Alte-Pinakothek-Muenchen 'http://www.cedon.de/Buecher/Museumspublikationen/').

Further publications of the Bavarian State Painting Collections can be found here.

Photo: Alexander Scharf

### Café

**OPENING HOURS** 
Daily 10 a.m. – 5.30 p.m. 
TUE, WED 10 a.m. – 7 p.m. 
MON closed

### House rules | Bag regulation

Bags up to the size DIN A 4 (no larger than 30 x 20 x 10 cm) may be taken into the museum. Please leave backpacks and larger bags at the cloakroom or deposit them in our deposit lockers. 

We kindly ask you consider the House rules (PDF), [House rules (PDF)](https://www.pinakothek.de/media/12399/download/2026_BSTGS_Hausordnung-Besucher_E.pdf?v=1), [Cloakroom rules (PDF)](https://www.pinakothek.de/media/7378/download/BStGS_Garderobenordnung_Engl.pdf?v=1) and the [Terms & Conditions](https://www.pinakothek.de/en/terms-and-conditions) that apply in all our museums. 

We kindly ask you to take note of them. Thank you very much!

Main Content

Die drei nahe der Alster gelegenen, markanten Gebäude der Hamburger Kunsthalle beherbergen eine der wichtigsten öffentlichen Kunstsammlungen Deutschlands. Die Kunsthalle ist eines der wenigen Häuser, die einen Rundgang durch acht Jahrhunderte Kunstgeschichte ermöglichen.

metadata.title: Welcome | Hamburger Kunsthalle
metadata.description: The three striking buildings of the Hamburger Kunsthalle, located close to the Alster, are home to one of the most important public art collections in Germany. The Kunsthalle is one of the few museums that offers a tour through eight centuries of art history.

## ENSEIGNANTS ET acteurs du champ socioculturel

## préparer votre venue

Pour préparer vos animations et/ou visites, nous vous proposons gratuitement plusieurs visites guidées relatives à nos collections, expositions ou au bâtiment.

Dans un second temps, si vous le souhaitez, une rencontre plus informelle a lieu avec une personne du service des publics pour répondre à vos questions et affiner vos projets.

### Visite guidée des collections permanentes du musée La Piscine

\> **Mer. 30 septembre 2026 à 14h30** 
Durée : 1h30 
_Inscription nécessaire, sur cette date, au plus tard le 21 sept. 2026_.

### Visite guidée des expositions

\> _[Ni Dieu, ni maître ! Arts et anarchie de Courbet à Banksy](https://www.roubaix-lapiscine.com/exposition/ni-dieu-ni-maitre-arts-et-anarchie-de-courbet-a-banksy/)_ 
**Sam. 10 ou mer. 14** **octobre 2026 à 14h30** 
Durée : 1h 

\> _[Préraphaélisme – Itinéraires féminins](https://www.roubaix-lapiscine.com/exposition/preraphaelisme-itineraires-feminins/)_ 
**Mer. 10 ou sam. 13 mars 2027 à 14h30** 
Durée : 1h

## \> Tarifs et Réservations

**Tarif**: Gratuit 

**Réservation obligatoire par mail** uniquement en précisant votre nom, prénom, numéro de portable, établissement et ville, ainsi que le niveau de votre classe ou la matière enseignée. 

_N.B. N’attendez pas ces dates pour réserver vos animations et parcours car nous ne serons peut-être plus en mesure de vous fournir des créneaux horaires._

## Concept Store

More than just a museum shop. The Museum's Concept Store offers an extensive selection of exhibition catalogs, art prints, and posters, alongside exclusive jewelry and a curated range of home accessories, including vases, tableware, textiles, and even selected furniture pieces.

The Concept Store can also be visited without a museum admission ticket. Simply speak to a member of staff at the ticket desk.

[Discover](https://www.museum-frieder-burda.de/en/concept-store/)

## Museum Frieder Burda

Frieder Burda was born in 1936 as the second son of publisher Franz Burda and entrepreneur Aenne Burda. A passion for art and an unerring eye for quality made him one of the most internationally important collectors of his generation. Founded by Frieder Burda in 2004, our museum is located on Baden-Baden's famous Lichtentaler Allee, directly adjacent to the Staatliche Kunsthalle Baden-Baden, to which it is connected by a glass bridge. Designed by renowned American architect Richard Meier, the building is often described as a “jewel in the park”. With an average of two to three temporary exhibitions each year, the museum has established itself as one of Europe's leading private museums and enjoys an outstanding international reputation.

[Learn More](https://www.museum-frieder-burda.de/en/museum/)

## A unique tour through European art history

in Zwinger

[18,00 € / Buy a Ticket](https://shop.skd.museum/tickets?eventfinder_museums=9)

© Staatliche Kunstsammlunegn Dresden, Foto: Oliver Killig

## Intro neu

The Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery) and the Skulpturensammlung bis 1800 (Sculpture Collection up to 1800) present their works together in the extensively renovated Semperbau am Zwinger.

[To the exhibition](https://gemaeldegalerie.skd.museum/en/exhibitions/gemaeldegalerie-alte-meister-old-masters-picture-gallery-and-skulpturensammlung-sculpture-collection-up-to-1800/)

exhibition of the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister at Semperbau am Zwinger

19/09/2026 —10/01/2027

### Correggio. Movingly Human

[Read more](https://gemaeldegalerie.skd.museum/en/exhibitions/correggio-movingly-human/) [Book tickets](https://shop.skd.museum/tickets?eventfinder_exhibitions=48)

© Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Foto: Jürgen Lösel

## Upcoming Events

## Zitat Goethe

> I entered this shrine, and my amazement exceeded any preconceived idea!

Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

## Systematically collected

Most of the principal works on display were collected within only five decades.

[Find out more](https://gemaeldegalerie.skd.museum/en/about-us/)

© Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Foto: David Pinzer

## From our Online Collection

- Skulpturensammlung bis 1800

## Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig

[Current\\ \\ **Art Within Four Walls**\\ \\ **Jewish Families and Their Collections in Leipzig**\\ \\ **30/09/2026 — 31/01/2027**\\ \\ The exhibition aims to revive memories of Jewish involvement in the arts in Leipzig and focuses on both the collections and the individual families and their stories.\\ \\ Max Pechstein, Portrait in Red, 1909, Hessisches Landesmuseum Darmstadt, photo: Wolfgang Fuhrmannek, CC BY-SA 4.0](https://mdbk.de/en/exhibitions/art-within-four-walls/)

#### Welcome

This video welcomes all visitors and aims to make your visit to the Museum easier by providing you with useful information. It gives a brief historical background as well as the main focuses of the MdbK collection. We provide information about accessibility, assistive technology and inclusive services. The video is interpreted in German Sign Language (DGS) and has German and English subtitles. 

You can find more information about accessibility at the MdbK >> [here](https://mdbk.de/en/information/#accessibility).

#### Free admission

To the permanent exhibitions on the first and second floors of the MdbK - this will apply from January 1, 2024 when the new municipal fee schedule comes into force. And for children and young people up to the age of 18, admission to the special exhibitions will also remain free. 

So come and visit the MdbK more often! We look forward to your visit.

#### Tenant Wanted

The MdbK is seeking an experienced manager to establish and independently operate an innovative museum shop. 
As an integral part of the visitor experience, the new shop should also serve as an attraction in its own right, drawing visitors beyond the museum itself. The goal is to create a contemporary space that combines art, design, retail, and interaction, and appeals to people of all ages.

[The full job posting can be found >> here.](https://mdbk.de/site/assets/files/1436/aufruf_interessensbekundung_mdbk_shop_2027.pdf) 
Application deadline: October 31, 2026​​​​​​​

[**Program 2027**](https://mdbk.de/en/museum/)

[In 2027, the MdbK will present three major special exhibitions that span a wide range of themes and artistic styles—from _Wolfgang Mattheuer_ to _Arnold Böcklin_ to _Grace Weaver._ The program will be complemented by two very different photography exhibitions: _Photography as Object_ and a presentation of photographs by _Ursula Arnold_. Next year, the MdbK will once again serve as a venue for the _Leipzig Children’s and Youth Art Exhibition_. The established series _Graphic Art in Focus_ will continue. More information is available](https://mdbk.de/en/museum/) [here](https://mdbk.de/en/exhibitions/).

#### MdbK \[Platz\]

On the studio terrace on the 2nd floor, the MdbK \[Platz\] invites visitors to play, draw, read and linger. Games, a puzzle, a drawing station and a reading corner are available to visitors during the museum’s opening hours. This free service is aimed at all ages and is suitable for individuals as well as groups. 

#### MdbK \[next;raum\]

The MdbK \[next;raum\] is a participatory and reflective space in the centre of the permanent exhibition. Together with actors from urban society, the aim is to critically discuss the collections, their presentation and mediation. 

[\>> Information on the current and two previous episodes can be found here.](https://mdbk.de/en/next-raum/)

#### Johann Kupetzky

The permanent exhibition features a portrait of Russian Tsar Peter the Great, on loan from the University of Leipzig’s art collection. It is displayed alongside a painting by Johann Kupetzky (1667–1740) from 1711/12. Comparing the two works offers a fascinating insight into studio practices of the early 18th century. You can learn more about this at the exhibition.

#### Programme of Art Mediation

[The art meditation programme for educational institutions and groups with information on our formats and events can be found _here_ (only in German).](https://mdbk.de/site/assets/files/1436/mdbk_kunstvermittlung_programmkatalog_2026_digital.pdf)

[\>> Click here for information about our guided tours and workshops for educational institutions](https://mdbk.de/en/information/)

[\>> Click here for information about our fall break program (only in German) with Dagesh on Tour](https://mdbk.de/site/assets/files/1436/mdbk_kunstvermittlung_herbstferienprogramm_2026_digital.pdf)

#### Open Studio

The Open Studio is the right place for anyone aged 12 and over who wants to draw and design or is simply looking for an exchange with other creative people. It is now open every Thursday from 3.30 pm to 6 pm and can be visited free of charge and without registration on the second floor of the MdbK.

#### MdbK \[Pocket Tour\]

The MdbK \[Pocket Tour\] was developed for museum visits with children, but can be used by anyone. It consists of a set of A5 cards, a clipboard, a bag with a mirror, a pencil, an hourglass and other objects for creative work. The cards contain questions and tasks about selected works of art at the MdbK, as well as additional information about the artists. The MdbK \[Pocket Tour\] can be borrowed from the Museum's ticket office and the cards can be taken home.

#### MdbK \[hubs\]

Currently, a total of six inclusive mediation stations for hearing, touching and seeing are installed at the MdbK, offering new access to works in the collection.

[\>> You can find more information about the project _here._](https://mdbk.de/en/hubs/)

#### Provenance research

The MdbK sees provenance research as a core task of its museum work and systematically examines its holdings on a project-related basis for cultural property seized as a result of Nazi persecution and for works of art that were expropriated during the Soviet occupation zone and the former GDR.

[\>> More here....](https://mdbk.de/en/provenance-research/)

#### Museum Square

[Nina Schuiki's 125 m long installation "Spring" will be presented to the public for the first time on June 12 at 5 pm in the Museum Square between MdbK and Katharinenstraße. From now on, it will be open to the public around the clock.](https://mdbk.de/en/museumskarree/)

#### MdbK \[in transit\]

From 2019 to 2025, the MdbK was part of the nationwide funding program 360° – Fund for Cultures of the New Urban Society. The designation MdbK \[in transit\] highlights the processes and outcomes initiated at the MdbK as part of the funding program, including the exhibitions _Re-Connect. Art and Conflict in Brotherland_ (May 18–Sept. 10, 2023), _Family Matters_ (June 19–Sept. 14, 2025), interventions in the collection presentation, as well as numerous events and a survey of non-visitors. Through the in\_transit working group, the team continues to work on diversifying staff, programming, and audiences even after the funding program has ended.

#### The Day After Tomorrow

The MdbK is funded by the Federal Cultural Foundation's “[The Day After Tomorrow - New Models for Cultural Institutions](https://uebermorgen-programm.de/en/home/)” program. Under the project title “What is missing - relationships as a future tool of the museum”, new ways of working will be tested at the MdbK until the end of 2026 and a concept for a community-creating place will be developed. The focus is on participation, art from the GDR and new uses for the museum architecture.

#### Sternburg Stiftung

The MdbK preserves the extensive collection of the Leipzig merchant Maximilian Freiherr Speck von Sternburg (1776-1856), which he assembled on his estate in Lützschena near Leipzig. It includes more than 200 paintings, numerous drawings and works of graphic art as well as a library.

[\>> Learn more here](https://mdbk.de/en/sternburg-stiftung/)

#### Evelyn Richter and Ursula Arnold Archive

The Evelyn Richter and Ursula Arnold Archive is a joint project of the Ostdeutsche Sparkassenstiftung and the Museum der bildenden Künste Leipzig. The works of the photographers are preserved and researched at the MdbK and made public through exhibitions and publications.

[\>> Find out more here.](https://mdbk.de/en/evelyn-richter-ursula-arnold-archiv/)

Accompanying the current exhibition, you can expect diverse and interesting events. **Browse through the Bucerius Book Shop on site or online** 
The Book Shop at the Bucerius Kunst Forum offers you a selection of specialist literature tailored to the current exhibition. Visit the Book Shop on site, before or after your visit to the exhibition, or order your favorites digitally in the new online Book Shop.

## Art from the Romantic period to the present day

in Albertinum

[14,00 € / Buy a Ticket](https://shop.skd.museum/hausticket-albertinum.html)

© Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Foto: Carina Sonntag

## \[Translate to English:\] Intro

From Caspar David Friedrich to Gerhard Richter: The exhibition in the Albertinum contains masterpieces from 1800 by the Romantic painters as well as 20th-century art and contemporary works.

[To the collection](https://albertinum.skd.museum/en/exhibitions/permanent-exhibition/)

exhibition of the Albertinum

31/10/2026 —22/08/2027

### The Great Drama. Auguste Rodin and the Debate over Modernism

[Read more](https://albertinum.skd.museum/en/exhibitions/the-great-drama-auguste-rodin-and-the-debate-over-modernism/) [Book tickets](https://shop.skd.museum/tickets?eventfinder_exhibitions=52)

© Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden, Foto: Anja Schneider

## Upcoming events

## Film

Load content from external provider

Privacy notice

When you play our YouTube or Vimeo videos, information about your use of YouTube or Vimeo is transmitted to the US operator and may be stored. In addition, external media such as videos or fonts are loaded and stored in your browser.

## Art from the Romantic period to the present day

Walking through the Albertinum is like opening a museum-sized art history reference work and leafing through its pages. With a range extending from Romanticism to the present, the Albertinum is a place where painting meets sculpture, East meets West and today meets tomorrow.

[Explore the permanent exhibition](https://albertinum.skd.museum/en/exhibitions/permanent-exhibition/)

© Albertinum | Galerie Neue Meister, Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden

## history

Founded in 1959, the Galerie Neue Meister is the youngest museum of the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden. Its collection initially came from the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister for which contemporary art was increasingly acquired after 1843. 
[History of the collection](https://albertinum.skd.museum/en/about-us/)

© SKD, Foto: David Pinzer

## Gerhard Richter

Gerhard  Richter is one of the most significant artists of the 20th and 21st centuries. His oeuvre covers a period of nearly five decades. The artist is connected to the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden and his birthplace Dresden in a unique way through the Gerhard Richter Archive, which was founded here and is named after him. 

[Gerhard Richter Archive](https://gerhard-richter-archiv.skd.museum/en/)

© Gerhard Richter 2018 (08022018), Foto: David Pinzer, Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden

### Renovation

The Staatsgalerie Stuttgart will be extensively modernized and renovated in the coming years.

For this reason, our **masterpieces of Classical Modernism****are currently not on view.** Starting February 20, 2027, they will be on display under the title “Simply the Best!” at the Kunstgebäude on Schlossplatz.

Thank you very much for your understanding regarding any restrictions!

## Explore Collection

IMMA is home to the National Collection of modern and contemporary art, with over 3,500 artworks by Irish and International artists. Our aim is to share and to develop the Collection for now and for the future. Search and explore the collection in your own time using the new collections archive.

## Membership

The IMMA MEMBERS programme provides a space to connect through culture and creativity. Join our inclusive community, composed of those seeking to experience the Museum in new ways. If you enjoy our grounds with your dog, are already familiar with our galleries, or are just looking for more creative inspiration in their lives, IMMA MEMBERS is for you. # English

Dear visitors,

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact [sprengel-museum@hannover-stadt.de](mailto:Sprengel-Museum@Hannover-Stadt.de) and +49 511 168-4 38 75. 
We look forward to your visit!

## CURRENT EXHIBITIONS

FROM 14.10.26: ANTON HENNING

**FROM 14.10.26**

The Sprengel Museum Hannover is delighted to announce a generous donation: the artist Anton Henning has given the museum nine additional works. From 14 October 2026, the new acquisitions will be on view for the first time alongside works already in the collection.

Anton Henning works across painting, sculpture, and installation. His practice repeatedly brings together different visual worlds while questioning the boundaries between art and everyday life. The presentation in Sprengel Focus centres on a recurring motif in his work: spaces that cannot be clearly read as either interiors or exteriors. Interiors meet landscapes, architecture meets ornamental imagery, and the familiar encounters the deliberately disorienting. The result is a body of work in which it is not always clear where a space begins or where it ends.

Curated by Johanna Adam

Image: Interieur mit Blumenstilleben und Früchten, No.17, 2024, Öl auf Leinwand, 240 x 260 cm; © VG Bild-Kunst, Bonn 2026; Foto: Herling/Herling/Werner, Sprengel Museum Hannover

## UPCOMING EXHIBITIONS

28.11.26 TO 21.2.27: NEVIN ALADAĞ. KURT SCHWITTERS PREIS 2026 DER NIEDERSÄCHSISCHEN SPARKASSENSTIFTUNG

**28.11.26 TO 21.2.27**

Nevin Aladağ has been awarded the Kurt Schwitters Prize 2026 by the Lower Saxony Sparkassen Foundation. The prize, now being conferred for the fifteenth time, carries a monetary award of €30,000 and includes a comprehensive solo exhibition at the Sprengel Museum Hannover. The award ceremony will take place in autumn 2026.

Born in 1972 in Van, Turkey, Aladağ grew up in Stuttgart and studied sculpture with Olaf Metzel at the Academy of Fine Arts Munich from 1994 to 2000. She currently lives in Berlin and has held a professorship in “Sculpture in Motion” at the Hochschule für Bildende Künste Dresden since 2019. Nevin Aladağ works across media. Her practice encompasses sculpture, installations, collages, reliefs, video and sound works, as well as performances. Everyday objects, situations, and actions often serve as starting points for her work. She is interested in the cultural and political meanings embedded in the origins and histories of these objects. By removing them from their original contexts, she alters their interpretation and reveals their ideological and political connotations. Another central focus of her work is music, dance, and play as expressions of cultural identity. In projects such as The Music Room, presented in 2017 at documenta in Athens, she combines musical instruments from around the world into sculptural works, performances, and wall reliefs.

Aladağ achieved international recognition through her participation in documenta 14 (Athens and Kassel) and the 57th Venice Biennale (2017). Her work has been presented in numerous solo exhibitions worldwide, including at the Max Ernst Museum Brühl (2024), as well as in Seoul, Munich, London, San Francisco, Hannover, Dresden, Linz, Basel, Berlin, and Istanbul.

**KURT SCHWITTERS PRIZE OF THE LOWER SAXONY SPARKASSEN FOUNDATION**

The Kurt Schwitters Prize aims to honor artists “whose work is distinguished by reference to Kurt Schwitters and is characterized by venturing into new areas of artistic form and imagination, or whose work contributes to the connection and integration of artistic disciplines.” The award is a key component of the Lower Saxony Sparkassen Foundation’s cultural support, which is marked by year-round engagement in the fields of visual arts, music, museums, and heritage preservation.

Curated by Stefan Gronert

Opening: 27.11.26, 7 p.m.

Image: Nevin Aladağ, Rendering, 2026

2.12.26 TO 7.2.27: HANNES MALTE MAHLER. RETROSPEKTIVE

**2.12.26 TO 7.2.27**

Hannes Malte Mahler is an artist whose work is as colorful and multifaceted as his heraldic animal—the chameleon. The range of his work is enormous, spanning painting, drawing, and photography, as well as object and performance art, all the way to installations featuring—or lacking—“particles” made of Styrodur, doodles, and other trifles. Added to this are digital drawings that Mahler—exploring the tension between art and commerce—transferred onto colorful T-shirts and tote bags in one of his latest major projects under the title “Mahlerwear. It is art”. At the end of 2026, the Sprengel Museum Hannover will dedicate a comprehensive retrospective to Hannes Malte Mahler, honoring the versatility and uniqueness of his artistic work.

Curated by Reinhard Spieler

Opening: 1.12.26, 7 p.m.

Image: Hannes Malte Mahler, Ohne Titel (Der Astronaut), nicht datiert, 160 x 120 cm, Öl auf Leinwand, Foto Birgit Streicher

## COLLECTION

FROM 17.5.26: MEIN LIEBER SCHWAN! DIE SAMMLUNG

**MEIN LIEBER SCHWAN!** 
**DIE SAMMLUNG** 
**FROM MAY 17th 2026** 

The Sprengel Museum Hannover shows a comprehensively reimagined presentation of its collection. Titled "Mein lieber Schwan!", the new display brings together more than 170 artistic positions from the 20th and 21st centuries across approximately 3,000 square metres and 20 newly designed galleries, creating unexpected encounters and fresh dialogues between artworks.

The presentation connects works of Classical Modernism with contemporary art, offering new perspectives on art history—not as a linear narrative, but as an open network of relationships, ruptures and rediscoveries. Highlights include major works by Max Beckmann, Pablo Picasso, Georg Baselitz, Isa Genzken, Hannah Höch, Bruce Nauman, Gerhard Richter, Karin Sander and Timm Ulrichs.

While the exhibition broadly follows a chronological structure, this narrative is repeatedly interrupted by thematic and aesthetic interventions. Familiar works are placed in unusual constellations, inviting visitors to experience art from new perspectives.

The title "Mein lieber Schwan!" (a German expression meaning "Good Gracious!"), borrowed from a work by Hanover-based artist Christiane Möbus, reflects the exhibition’s guiding principle: curiosity as a principle and surprise as a method.

Thematic sections range from the avant-gardes of modernism to questions of materiality, the body, memory and society, culminating in open-ended constellations of contemporary art. Works by Kurt Schwitters, Niki de Saint Phalle, Joseph Beuys, Thomas Schütte and Kader Attia open up diverse perspectives on art and its social significance.

The new collection presentation is accompanied by a newly developed educational programme featuring an audio guide, exhibition booklet and interactive formats such as the “Kritzelmobil”, which encourages visitors to explore the exhibition in a playful and experimental way.

To mark the opening on 17 May 2026, the museum will host a full-day programme of guided tours, workshops and special activities. The exhibition invites audiences to rediscover the collection as a space for questions, encounters and unexpected connections.

Curated by Inka Schube and Katharina Hermann

Image: Schad, Christian, Lotte (Die Berlinerin), 1927/28, Öl auf Holz, 66,2 × 54,5 cm, Sprengel Museum Hannover, Kunstbesitz der Landeshauptstadt Hannover; © VG Bild Kunst, Bonn 2026, Foto: Herling/Herling/Werner, Sprengel Museum Hannover

FROM 23.4.23: ABENTEUER ABSTRAKTION

**ABENTEUER ABSTRAKTION** 
**FROM 23.4.23**

In "Abenteuer Abstraktion", the Sprengel Museum Hannover is showing a significant part of its collection in the museum’s newly fitted rooms. The selection provides an overview of major manifestations and developments in non-representational art from the beginning of the 20th century to the present day. The starting point and focus of the tour are the reconstructions of El Lissitzky’s Cabinet of the Abstract (1927) and Kurt Schwitters’ Merz Construction (1933). Both rooms, which previously existed in Hannover, embody influential stages in abstract art and allow the visitor to directly experience the interplay of colour and form.

In addition to outstanding works by Schwitters and Lissitzky, Classical Modernism is represented by works by Piet Mondrian, Hans Arp and Paul Klee, among others. From the post-war period are works by, among others, Willi Baumeister, Pierre Soulages and K.O. Götz. These lead on to contemporary artists, such as Pia Fries, Pipilotti Rist and Wolfgang Tillmans. Awaiting discovery in the 18 rooms of "The Adventure of Abstraction" are cabinet of graphic works, expansive media artworks and abstract films from the early days of the medium.

Image: Reconstruction of Kurt Schwitters' Merzbau, Photo: Herling/Herling/Werner, Sprengel Museum Hannover

FROM 23.4.23: ARTISTS IN HANNOVER UNDER NATIONAL SOCIALISM

**ARTISTS IN HANNOVER UNDER NATIONAL SOCIALISM** 
**FROM 23.4.23**

On the museum’s mezzanine floor, another area opens up that takes a look at Hannover artists and art from 1933 to 1945. Taking nine people as examples and tracing historical events, the exhibition illuminates the situation of art and artists under National Socialism and asks how the political conditions impacted on the institutions and artists’ lives and work, museum staff and collectors. Finally, we investigate the extent to which the Nazi past continues to affect the museum to this day.

Image: Artists in Hannover under National Socialism, Photo: Herling/Herling/Werner, Sprengel Museum Hannover

## ARCHIVE

1.8. TO 1.11.26: ZWISCHEN WIRKLICHKEIT UND TRAUM. OTTO GLEICHMANN UND DER EXPRESSIONISMUS IN HANNOVER

**1.8. TO 1.11.26**

Otto Gleichmann (Mainz 1887–1963 Hannover) moved to Hannover after the First World War, where he remained until his death. He is regarded as a major solitary figure among the younger generation of German Expressionists. Despite his considerable success during the 1910s and 1920s, he has since fallen largely into obscurity. This exhibition seeks to rediscover an important painter and draughtsman whose impact extended far beyond the city of Hannover.

Gleichmann’s oeuvre is marked by humanitarian pathos and profound sensitivity; his central subject is the human figure. His stylized, unmistakable faces with wide, cat-like eyes bear witness to the horrors of war he experienced firsthand. Enchanted, often otherworldly figures wander through densely populated urban spaces or appear in the lively environments of cabarets and circuses. Human relationships—solitude, proximity, and the complexities of social interaction—are explored in multifigural compositions imbued with psychological nuance. Throughout his career, Gleichmann focused predominantly on figural scenes in a wide range of configurations, complemented only occasionally by depictions of animals—especially cats and horses—by floral still lifes, and by a small number of landscapes.

The development of his motifs over nearly five decades can be traced with exceptional clarity: from the dark, suffering corporeality of his early Expressionist period, to a more relaxed and introspective calmness beginning in the mid-1920s, and ultimately to the luminous, lyrical, yet still subtly agitated touch of his postwar years. In these later works, nature and figure increasingly merge, arriving at a distinctly personal freedom of line, color, and light.

For the first time since 1987, this Hannover-based artist is being honored in a major retrospective, featuring approximately 180 loans as well as works from the Sprengel Museum’s own collection. A catalogue will accompany the exhibition.

Curated by Karin Orchard

Image: Otto Gleichmann, Porträt Hans Koch, 1919 | Öl auf Baumwolle, Höhe × Breite: 76,5 × 70 cm Sprengel Museum Hannover, Hannover

1.7. TO 4.10.26: PAUL MPAGI SEPUYA. IM BLICK DES BEGEHRENS.

**1.7. TO 4.10.26**

Paul Mpagi Sepuya (\*1982, San Bernardino, California) is regarded as one of the most significant voices in contemporary photography in the United States. The exhibition at the Sprengel Museum Hannover marks the artist’s first major solo presentation at a German museum. It reveals how Sepuya, in his poetically composed works, deconstructs the conventions of classical portraiture, employing the camera as both an instrument and a subject, while simultaneously creating spaces of intimacy, fragmentation, and reflection. Through the deliberate use of mirrors, fabrics, and studio elements, Sepuya interrogates the mechanisms of looking—who observes, who is observed, and how photographic intimacy is constructed.

Sepuya’s practice is shaped by queer perspectives, a conscious engagement with visibility, and a profound examination of the photographic act itself. His images are not mere representations but performative processes—open, sensitive, and attentive to the power structures embedded in the medium.

Developed jointly by the Sprengel Museum Hannover and the Fotomuseum Winterthur (28 February–14 June 2026), the exhibition places Sepuya’s artistic, medial, and political concerns at its center—particularly his engagement with Blackness, the body, and spatiality. The artist himself describes his aims as “thinking anew about the structures of photography, portraiture, and queer sociality” and “recognizing the fundamental position of Blackness as material—or Blackness and darkness as a place from which and into which one looks” (Paul Sepuya).

Curated by Stefan Gronert

Image: Paul Mpagi Sepuya, Mirror Study (0X5A7394), Archival pigment print, 2017 © Paul Mpagi Sepuya

13.6. TO 26.9.26: KUNSTPREIS HANNES MALTE MAHLER - IT IS ART®. FARZANE VAZIRITABAR

**13.6. TO 27.9.26**

The “Hannes Malte Mahler Art Prize – it is art®” is awarded every four years by the non-profit association feinkunst e.V. in cooperation with the Sprengel Museum Hannover. Established in 2020, the prize commemorates the Hanover-based artist Hannes Malte Mahler (1968–2016), who died tragically in 2016 and was a master student of Marina Abramović. With prize money of 15,000 euros as well as a project and production budget of up to 105,000 euros, it is one of the most highly endowed art prizes in Germany. The funding is aimed at both emerging and established artists and includes an invitation to realize a project in the urban space of Hanover as well as in the premises of feinkunst e.V. and the Sprengel Museum Hannover.

The recipient of the “Hannes Malte Mahler Art Prize 2024 – it is art®” is the artist Farzane Vaziritabar, born in 1987 in Yazd, Iran. 11.4. TO 5.7.26: HORST ANTES. EINE SAMMLUNG

**11.4. TO 5.7.26**

Horst Antes is considered one of the pioneers of New Figuration in Germany. His iconic “head-footers” (“Kopffüßler”), his consistent exploration of the human figure in space, and his house archetypes have brought him international recognition since the 1960s.

The exhibition offers a comprehensive insight into the artist's multifaceted body of work, ranging from early painterly experiments to later groups of works. At its core is the important collection bequeathed to the Sprengel Museum in 1988 by Wolf and Ursula Hermann and continuously expanded through the funds of their foundation. Today, it represents the most extensive public museum collection of works by Antes.

The exhibition features paintings, prints, and sculptures that vividly convey the quiet intensity, formal rigor, and lasting relevance of Antes’s visual language. All approximately 80 paintings from the collection are on display, spanning his artistic production from the early 1960s to the present day. The works have been arranged by Antes himself in a highly specific way, forming a kind of installation.

The presentation is complemented by the monumental seven-part sculptural ensemble Garden of the Seven Monuments of Pleasure, which Antes created for the Federal Garden Show in Karlsruhe in 1967 and which is now located in Aachen.

“Horst Antes. A Collection” will open together with an installation by Kaloki Nyamai.

Curated by Reinhard Spieler

6.9.25 TO 14.2.26: NIKI. KUSAMA. MURAKAMI. LOVE YOU FOR INFINITY

**21.5. TO 28.9.25**

From September 2025 to February 2026, the Sprengel Museum is presenting the exhibition "Love you for infinity" – a major exhibition highlight that shows works by Niki de Saint Phalle together with works by Yayoi Kusama and Takashi Murakami for the first time. The occasion for this special show is the donation of over 400 works that Niki de Saint Phalle made to the Sprengel Museum in 2000. The exhibition ranges from Niki de Saint Phalle's "shooting pictures" and the famous "Nanas" to Kusama's immersive "Infinity Rooms" installations and Murakami's pop wallpaper. It combines painting, sculpture, installation and film.

Similarities as well as differences between the artistic styles are revealed in the synopsis. On over 2,000 square metres, surprising connections emerge between the large-format works: from exuberant joie de vivre to existential threats, from feminism and female self-assertion to male dominance.

"Love you for infinity" is the first exhibition to combine works by Niki de Saint Phalle with those of Japanese artists Yayoi Kusama (born 1929) and Takashi Murakami (born 1962). All three artists share an enthusiasm for colourful, expressive worlds of colour and forms. Their visual language transcends the boundaries of art, pop culture and commerce and deals with central themes such as art and consumption, life and death as well as sexuality and trauma – each work in its own way.

**BACKGROUND**

Niki de Saint Phalle achieved international fame with her Nana figures, which were first exhibited in public spaces in Hanover in 1974. Hotly debated at the time, the striking sculptures still characterize the cityscape today. These and other expansive sculptures and paintings articulate a particularly memorable, popular, colorful and life-affirming visual language that is also politically charged. The same can be said for Kusama's work. The situation is similar with Murakami, whose commercialized visual language has developed an unmistakable oeuvre with a high recognition factor: What colourful Nanas are to Niki de Saint Phalle, polka dots are to Yayoi Kusama and stylized colourful flowers in emoji-style are to Takashi Murakami.

13.4.19 TO 26.10.25: ELEMENTARTEILE. GRUNDBAUSTEINE DES SPRENGEL MUSEUM HANNOVER UND SEINER KUNST

**13.4.19 TO 26.10.25**

To mark its 40th anniversary, the Sprengel Museum Hannover presents the exhibition ELEMENTARY PARTS in its Extension Building. What are the core components of an institution? What is art, what is it made of, what does it relate to, and what is it about? In ten thematic galleries, the Sprengel Museum Hannover examines itself as an institution and its collection through these fundamental questions.

What role does colour play as one of the basic building blocks of art? Which materials do artists use, and according to which principles of form and composition do they work? What forms of reality do works situated between conceptual art, abstraction and figuration refer to? Which themes and contents are significant, which stories are told, and how is history reflected in art? ELEMENTARY PARTS brings together more than 150 works from the 20th century and contemporary art, presenting an impressive range of forms of expression in painting, sculpture, graphic art, photography and film by artists including Max Beckmann, Louise Bourgeois, Grethe Jürgens, Niki de Saint Phalle, Pablo Picasso and Gerhard Richter.

**The Sprengel Museum Hannover**

On his 70th birthday, 17 April 1969, Bernhard Sprengel announced that he and his wife Margrit wished to donate their joint collection to the City of Hannover. Ten years later, the “Kunstmuseum Hannover mit Sammlung Sprengel” opened; in 1984, it was renamed the “Sprengel Museum Hannover”. A second phase of construction was completed in 1992, followed by an Extension Building in 2015.

The Sprengel Museum Hannover houses all works created after 1900 from the collections of the City of Hannover, the State of Lower Saxony and the Sprengel Collection. These are complemented by holdings from the Kurt and Ernst Schwitters Foundation, the Kurt Schwitters Archive, the Lower Saxony Foundation for Savings Banks, the Rudolf Jahns Foundation, the Bernhard Sprengel and Friends Foundation, the Hannover Re Foundation, the Fritz Behrens Foundation and various other foundations, held as permanent loans.

22.2 TO 15.6.25: GRETHE JÜRGENS. RETROSPEKTIVE

**22.2 TO 15.6.25**

The comprehensive retrospective of Grethe Jürgens at the Sprengel Museum Hannover explores the work of an important representative of the New Objectivity movement of the 1920s. For the first time, the exhibition presents part of her estate, comprising more than 370 works from various periods of her artistic career. Marking the 2025 anniversary year of New Objectivity, the retrospective brings together around 150 works, complemented by numerous documents. The exhibition offers a rare opportunity to discover the full breadth of the work of Grethe Jürgens, an artist who for a long time remained in the shadow of other representatives of New Objectivity. The accompanying catalogue, published by Snoeck, features contributions by various authors that provide insights into her work and life and fully acknowledge her significance as an artist.

## Career and Style

Born in Osnabrück in 1899, Jürgens began studying graphic art in Hannover, where she encountered artists who would later become known as the “New Objectivity in Hannover”. From an early stage, she devoted herself to distinctive portraits and urban landscapes. She later developed her characteristic visual language through matter-of-fact, detached depictions of workers and marginalised groups, characterised by sober realism and a cool, unemotional gaze. Her works are free from accusation or condemnation, yet attentively reveal social tensions and the challenges of life on the margins of society.

## Career and Challenges

Jürgens’ artistic breakthrough came with her first exhibitions from 1928 onwards. She regularly participated in exhibitions in Hannover, and her works were acquired by public collections. After the National Socialists came to power, she was required to register with the Reich Chamber of Fine Arts, but she was not a member of the Nazi Party and her works escaped confiscation. She adapted to the changed circumstances, turning her attention to landscapes and plants and developing her style of “Unkrautmalerei” (“weed painting”), characterised by seemingly innocuous motifs from nature.

Her “Rubble Paintings”, created in the aftermath of the destruction of Hannover, are unique in their striking depiction of ruins and the beginnings of reconstruction. These works reflect both the horror of war and the hope of rebuilding. From the 1950s onwards, her reputation grew again, and she increasingly came to be recognised as an artist of New Objectivity. Jürgens subsequently moved towards abstract art, creating series such as the “Line Compositions” and the “Kaleidoscopes”. Yet her willingness to experiment remained undiminished well into old age, even as her work increasingly oscillated between abstraction and figurative motifs.

# Your Visit

**Contact**

### We look forward to your visit!

Tickets are available at the ticket desk on-site.

#### Goodbye Franz Marc, welcome Picasso!

Our Franz Marc masterpieces, including ‘The White Cat’, will be on tour as loans until spring/summer 2027. In their place, two paintings by Picasso from the Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen will be our guests from 5 September 2026 until late February 2027.

[Further information](https://www.kunstmuseum-moritzburg.de/en/welcome-picasso/)

#### **Visitor address and postal address**

Kunstmuseum Moritzburg Halle (Saale) 
Friedemann-Bach-Platz 5 
06108 Halle (Saale)

T: +49 345 21259-0 
F: +49 345 20299-90

[kunstmuseum-moritzburg@kulturstiftung-st.de](https://www.kunstmuseum-moritzburg.de/en/your-visit/#)

#### Visitor Services

T: +49 345 21259-40 
Mon–Thu 9 am–12 pm & 2 pm–3:30 pm | Fri 9 am–12 pm

**Directions**

[route planner](https://www.google.de/maps/place/51.486499,11.963903)

#### **Visitor address**

Kunstmuseum Moritzburg Halle (Saale) 
Friedemann-Bach-Platz 5 
06108 Halle (Saale)

#### **Barrier-free access**

Our museum is fully accessible. For people with physical disabilities, the lift and stairlift provide step-free access to all exhibitions and the cloakroom and toilet areas. A wheelchair is available at the museum ticket desk.

#### Parking

**Friedemann-Bach-Platz parking** 
73 parking spaces directly in front of the museum

[Parking map Halle (Saale)](http://geodienste.halle.de/halgis/?s=Marktplatz&n=1&d=2500&l=parken)

#### Coaches

**Friedemann-Bach-Platz parking** 
Two coach parking spaces directly in front of the museum

[Coach parking map Halle (Saale)](https://www.google.com/maps/d/viewer?mid=1a0oTrrmEQDxPMK5t18VvLlhTnUo&msa=0&ll=51.485378843135734%2C11.97146837470018&spn=0.112441%2C0.220757&z=14)

#### Local and long-distance transport

You can get here on local and long-distance trains via Halle central station. The town of Halle an der Saale has excellent links to the new ICE express train line between Berlin and Munich, and the Central German rapid-transit S-Bahn service. From the central station, tram 7 (Kröllwitz) takes you straight to the Moritzburgring tram stop. From there, it is just a couple of steps to the entrance of the art museum.

**Prices**

### Admission Tickets

#### Ticket Permanent Exhibition

**8 euros | reduced 5 euros** 
This ticket allows you to visit the permanent exhibition and the temporary exhibitions “Fire & Form. Ceramics of Modernism” and “Maria Gerbaulet. Gustav-Weidanz-Prize 2025”.

#### Annual Ticket

**50 Euro | reduced 30 Euro** 
This ticket is only available at the museum ticket desk on-site. Holders of an Annual Ticket can reserve a ticket for the permanent or special exhibitions by acquiring a free ticket in our online shop. Entitlement to the free ticket must be shown at the entrance.

### Buy a ticket

Tickets are available at the ticket desk on-site.

### Reductions | Free admission

Free admission for: children up to the age of 18, school pupils, apprentices, students etc.

Reduced admission for: group of more than 10 persons (per person), recipients of Citizen's benefit (Bürgergeld), severely handicapped people etc.

[Information on concessionary admission prices (PDF-file, German,90 KB)](https://www.kulturstiftung-st.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Kunstmuseum_Moritzburg/PDF-Dateien/A_Ihr_Besuch/KunstmuseumMoritzburgHalleSaale_Eintritt_Ermaessigungen.pdf)

**Guides**

#### Individual tours

Want to get to know the museum and its collections better – along with your friends, co-workers or a tour group? We will be happy to put together a package to suit your private tour.

[Further information](https://www.kunstmuseum-moritzburg.de/en/experience-art/#collapseBox-28824)

#### Public tours

Public guided tours of the permanent exhibition and special exhibitions take place regularly in German. Current times can be found in our events calendar_._

Becoming a Friend of Butler Gallery is your opportunity to be part of a world of incredible art and creativity, and to support an organisation that is pivotal to the development of the visual arts in Ireland.

# Drogheda's Municipal Art Gallery

Highlanes Gallery is a public art gallery and visual arts exhibition centre in Drogheda, Ireland.The gallery opened its doors on October 4, 2006 and was the culmination of many years planning to deliver a dedicated visual arts space for the Irish north east region, of an International standard in terms of design, management and environmental control.

### Explore the Collection

Originally developed by artist Bea Orpen, Husband Terry Trench, and the 1947 Museum Committee, the Drogheda Municipal Art Collection has grown to include more than 100 artworks. From 18th Century paintings to modern sculptures, the collection continues to grow and to showcase a multitude of artist styles & artworks.

 ## Limerick City Gallery of Art

Limerick City Gallery of Art (LCGA) invites you to see the best of contemporary art through the exhibition program and to enjoy our extensive collection of Irish art. LCGA is the largest contemporary art gallery in the Mid-Western Region, annually exhibiting national and international artists in a diverse exhibition program.

LCGA is in the historic Carnegie Building on the grounds to the People's Park, in Limerick City.

Where art and ideas meet across the centuries...

Crawford Art Gallery is one of Ireland’s National Cultural Institutions, charged with the care of over 3,500 diverse artworks from the National Collection, from 18th century Irish and European painting and sculpture, through to contemporary video installations.

In 2024, Crawford Art Gallery embarked on an ambitious redevelopment project, Transforming Crawford Art Gallery, to ensure the gallery’s historic buildings in the heart of Cork city are conserved and enhanced for generations to come. 

From 22 September 2024, Crawford Art Gallery is temporarily closed to the public to facilitate these redevelopment works. Gallery staff continue to work behind the scenes, caring for the collection, organising an offsite programme of Learn & Explore events, and preparing for reopening in 2028. 

For news and updates on Transforming Crawford Art Gallery, the best way to stay in touch during our closure is by signing up to our newsletter or following our social media accounts.

## Art & Artists

During our refurbishment period, discover our rich collection of Irish and international art from the 19th century to today online. Highlights include Impressionist masterpieces, the unique Francis Bacon studio, dazzling stained glass by Harry Clarke and powerful paintings by Sean Scully.

[Go to Art & Artists](https://hughlane.ie/art-artists/)

## Explore & Learn

Our Explore and Learn programmes are operating citywide in myriad locations during our refurbishment period. The team create dynamic, innovative and inspiring programmes of creativity and art appreciation for people of all ages and interests.

[Go to Explore & Learn](https://hughlane.ie/explore-learn/)

Explore our extraordinary collection of modern and contemporary art through our online collection.

# Discover the wonders of the Hunt Museum

A world class collection of art and antiquities

2,500 objects. 5,000 years. Infinite stories.

- [VISIT](https://www.huntmuseum.com/visit)
- [BOOK](https://www.huntmuseum.com/visit/book-tickets/)

## Opening Times

- Tuesday – Saturday: 10am – 5pm
- Sunday: 11am – 5pm
- Monday: Closed
- An average visit lasts between 45 minutes to 1 hour

[Visit](https://www.huntmuseum.com/visit/)

## Tickets

- Under 16s go FREE with accompanying adults
- Adult: €12.50
- Concessions: €10.00
- Group (+5 adults): €10.00 per person

[Book](https://www.huntmuseum.com/visit/book-tickets/)

The Custom House 
Rutland Street, Limerick 
V94 EV8A

[VIEW MAP](https://www.huntmuseum.com/visit/location-opening-times/)

## The finest Van Gogh collection

The Kröller-Müller Museum has the finest Van Gogh collection in the world. Immerse yourself in the world of this Dutch master.

[Discover the Van Gogh collection](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en/about-the-collection/van-gogh-collection)

## Stroll through the sculpture garden

Explore one of the largest sculpture gardens in Europe and stroll among sculptures by artists such as Barbara Hepworth, Jean Dubuffet, and Marta Pan.

[More about the sculpture garden](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en/about-the-collection/sculpture-garden)

## Discover the collection

Take a stroll past the highlights of the Helene Kröller-Müller collection, from old masters to modern art.

[Search the collection](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en/collection) [About the collection](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en/about-the-collection)

## Exhibition _Van Gogh, All Our Paintings_

For the first time since 1984, you can see all the paintings by Vincent van Gogh from the Kröller-Müller collection. An absolute must for Van Gogh enthusiasts!

[More about the exhibition](https://www.krollermuller.nl/en/what-s-on/exhibitions/van-gogh-all-our-paintings)

- # Discover the Life and Work of Vincent van Gogh

 See Vincent van Gogh’s iconic paintings at the Van Gogh Museum and be moved by his amazing life story. Buy tickets at tickets.vangoghmuseum.com.

 [Book tickets](https://tickets.vangoghmuseum.com/?promo_creative=button&promo_pos=www-vgm&promo_name=tickets&promo_id=www-vgm-tickets-button) [Donate](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/about/support-the-museum)

- Now on view

 ## Whistler. Dandy and Disruptor

 James McNeill Whistler is one of the most important artists of the 19th century. Discover the first retrospective of his work in the Netherlands.

 [Discover more](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/exhibitions/whistler)

- ## Van Gogh’s Masterpieces

 Explore Vincent van Gogh’s famous masterpieces in the permanent exhibition. Get up close to iconic masterpieces such as ‘The Potato Eaters,’ ‘Almond Blossom’, and ‘Sunflowers’.

 [Discover more](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/the-permanent-collection-van-goghs-masterpieces)

- Now on view

 ## Yoshitoshi. Master of the Moon

 One hundred prints, one hundred stories, and always the moon. Discover historical figures, warriors, lovers and mythical beings, and how Yoshitoshi brings them to life in powerful, colourful prints.

 [Find out more](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on/exhibitions/yoshitoshi-master-of-the-moon)

- Story

 ## Inspiration from Japan

 Why did Vincent van Gogh love Japanese prints and what did he learn from them? Discover how Japanese prints changed his art for good.

 [Read the story](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/art-and-stories/stories/inspiration-from-japan)

- ## Explore further:

 - [See what’s on](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/visit/whats-on)
 - [Explore the art in the collection](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en/collection)

# Mauritshuis

## Welcome to the Mauritshuis

Home to 'Girl with a Peal Earring'

[Book tickets](https://tickets.mauritshuis.nl/event/mauritshuis-n57qyi?utm_campaign=OYhLOaSx&utm_source=shareable_link)

[Plan your visit](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/visit)

[Now on view: Thyssen-Bornemisza ❤️ Mauritshuis​ - Masterpieces from Madrid](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/what-s-on/exhibitions/thyssen-bornemisza)

[Step back in time at the Prince William V Gallery.](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/what-s-on/always-on-show/prince-william-v-gallery)

The best from the age of Rembrandt and Vermeer

## Opening hours

##### Mauritshuis

Monday 13:00 - 18:00

Tuesday - Sunday 10:00 - 18:00

##### Prince William V Gallery

Monday Closed

Tuesday - Sunday 12 am - 5 pm

[More opening hours](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/visit)

## Discover the collection through art stories

There is a lot to tell about the paintings of the Mauritshuis. Together with experts from outside the museum, we're gathering the most engaging stories about our collection. 

[View Art Stories](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/our-collection/stories)

[Art story\\ \\ **The most famous girl in the world**\\ \\ People travel to The Hague from all over the world to see Johannes Vermeer’s Girl with a Pearl Earring in the flesh. Or dream of coming here. But why is she so famous? We don’t know why exactly. We do have some theories, but we can’t explain it entirely. And maybe we don’t really want to – a little mystery suits the Girl.](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/our-collection/stories/the-girl-our-most-famous-painting)

[Art story\\ \\ **Why Rembrandt was the most exciting artist of the 17th century**\\ \\ Rembrandt is the Netherlands’ best-known artist. But why is that? What makes his paintings so special?](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/our-collection/stories/rembrandt)

[Art story\\ \\ **The Goldfinch**\\ \\ The little bird that Carel Fabritius painted in 1654 has flown around the world. Just what is it that makes this rather ordinary European goldfinch so attractive?](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/our-collection/stories/the-goldfinch)
